# Lambda

**Parity grade: A** · SDK `aws-sdk-go-v2/service/lambda@v1.112.2` · last audited 2026-10-07 (`51ea2ace0`) · protocol REST-JSON

## Coverage

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Feature families | 11 (11 ok) |
| Known gaps | 1 |
| Structural gaps (can't be emulated) | 11 |
| Deferred items | 0 |
| Resource leaks | ok |

### Known gaps

- --lambda-isolation=firecracker is rejected at startup: no firecracker binary is installed on the build host, so no microVM runner exists. Design: export the function image with `docker export` into an ext4 rootfs, boot it under firecracker with a configured kernel image (--lambda-firecracker-kernel), and reach the Runtime API over vsock (or a TAP device) instead of the docker bridge. Needs /dev/kvm access and a firecracker binary to build and test (gopherstack-cefu7.7).

### Structural gaps

These do not block an A grade — no implementation could produce real data here because the underlying data source cannot exist in an emulator.

- Stream ESM ParallelizationFactor/TumblingWindowInSeconds: records are hashed by partition key (Kinesis) or item key (DynamoDB) onto N ordered lanes, drained concurrently; a retrying lane pauses reads for the whole shard, tumbling state is kept per lane, and windows close on the clock only once the shard is caught up (Kinesis's up-to-2-minute idle wait is not modeled).
- ESM SchemaRegistryErrorCount and EventPollerUnit metrics: no Glue/Confluent schema-registry integration or poller-unit billing model exist to measure (ProvisionedPollers is emitted for SQS mappings with ProvisionedPollerConfig).
- Kafka ESM LoggingConfig DEBUG offsets are logged on every commit, not once a minute, and omit endOffset; INFO/WARN omit securityProtocol, saslMechanism, networkConfig, assignedPartitions (no VPC/auth/rebalance model).
- Invoke TenantId is validated (required for PER_TENANT, rejected otherwise) but does not route to a tenant-dedicated execution environment: one environment pool per function.
- Kafka ESM: MSK sources are polled only when services/kafka runs a real broker (--kafka-engine=docker); metadata-only MSK clusters stay unpolled with a warning, and MSK auth settings (IAM/SCRAM/TLS) are ignored (gopherstack-ce985).
- MQ ESM: Amazon MQ sources are polled only when services/mq runs a real broker (--mq-engine=docker); metadata-only brokers stay unpolled with a warning. ActiveMQ is consumed over STOMP (AWS uses OpenWire/JMS), so brokerInTime is the message timestamp and messageType is inferred from STOMP content-length; one queue per mapping (Queues[0]); no TLS; the BASIC_AUTH secret must be JSON with username/password keys (the Lambda guide does not show its layout) and is read from services/secretsmanager in the secret ARN's region.
- Kafka ESM (self-managed): SourceAccessConfigurations (SASL/SCRAM, mTLS, TLS root CA, VPC) are ignored -- only plaintext brokers are reachable -- and per-partition concurrency is not modeled (gopherstack-ce985).
- ESM SQS concurrency: with ScalingConfig.MaximumConcurrency (2..1000) or ProvisionedPollerConfig the mapping runs concurrent batch workers (cap = MaximumConcurrency, or pollers x 10 within Min..Max, doubling/halving with backlog). Without either, a mapping still processes one batch per tick, whereas AWS starts at 5 concurrent batches and scales up. Kafka/MSK ProvisionedPollerConfig and EventPollerUnit are stored only; the emulator's Kafka worker is one consumer per mapping.
- UpdateFunctionCode SourceKMSKeyArn is stored and echoed only: no deployment-package encryption exists to apply the key to. Function KMSKeyArn encryption of environment variables is real (see the 2026-10-25 note); KMS Decrypt grants/key policies are not consulted (the emulated KMS has no principal for Lambda), so KMSAccessDeniedException arises only for a non-encrypt/decrypt key or a ciphertext/encryption-context mismatch.
- FileSystemConfigs: mount-target subnet/AZ and security-group NFS reachability are checked only as VPC membership. EFSIO/EFSMount* exceptions are never raised. Deleting an access point a function references is allowed, as no EFS error documents otherwise. The access point PosixUser is applied by running the whole function process as that uid:gid (+ supplementary gids), not per-file NFS identity squashing, and RootDirectory CreationInfo ownership is chowned only when the emulator itself runs privileged (permissions are always applied).
- Capacity providers (Lambda Managed Instances): execution environments are logical slots over the function's single local container, not separate containers or EC2 instances. Invocations are admitted per environment (PerExecutionEnvironmentMaxConcurrency; unset defaults per vCPU follow the runtime guides: nodejs 64, java/dotnet 32, python 16; runtimes with no documented default, e.g. provided/go/ruby, are uncapped per environment), environments scale out to FunctionScalingConfig max and the provider MaxVCpuCount (default 400), min defaults to 3; ScalingMode/ScalingPolicies, InstanceRequirements, VpcConfig and throttle-reason metrics (CPUThrottles/MemoryThrottles) are accepted and echoed but do not influence routing, and exhausted capacity is a synchronous 429 where AWS scales out asynchronously.
